summary: A brick light on Beaver Island's south bluff, lit in 1851 amid the Mormon colony, kept by Tip Miller and Dominick Gallagher, dark since 1962 and now a museum site.

notes_for_editor: Main narrative sources are LighthouseFriends and Terry Pepper (copyrighted, paraphrased) plus Williams 1905, Light-House Board reports, and the Beaver Island Archive (a compilation of secondary summaries; the NRHP PDF is not digitised, so the nomination is cited only as summarized by the Archive). Disagreements stated in the text: first lit 1851/1852; 1858 rebuild cause (toppled 1857 vs deterioration); lamps (10 vs 14) and dwelling size; fog signal building 1910 vs 1915; oil vapor 1916 vs 1917; radiobeacon north vs east; telephone line 1953 (Pepper) vs 1943 Courier (Archive); automation 1958 vs 1962; hunting-lodge dates. Williams calls Loaney the 'second keeper' but USLHS has Chidester and Lobsdell before Looney. LighthouseFriends's 'next two keepers were Strangites' is not tied to names; the text says so. Roster lines are the USLHS lines; Lewis N. Allard (second assistant 1928-1933) is only in LighthouseFriends; Blakeslee and Bedford only in Williams. USLHS has Walters 1932-1938; LF leaves 1938 blank. The fog-signal hours in the LHB text were read from OCR sentence text, not tables. The siren-hours/fiscal year for the 1899 and 1901 volumes is labelled by the volume's year, check fiscal-year if used. The 1916 Bulletin item lists 'Beaver Island, Straits of Mackinac' among oil to incandescent oil vapor changes; it is matched to this station by name and by the 1916 LF date. Homans letter is cited second-hand via LighthouseFriends. The Dec 1900 Squaw Island crew names (Shields, McCauley) also appear in this roster but are not linked here. The BIHS claim of a 'two miles east' misplacement and 1954 Eisenhower order appears in no other source. Newspaper search (Chronicling America, Michigan 1851-1890) timed out and was not used. 'Dominick Gallagher' singer identification rests on the Archive; dates unsettled there.
